title: Credit Limit Override Lost in Migration — Customer Escalation
scenario_text:
Ironforge Manufacturing receives an urgent complaint from a long-standing customer whose orders are being blocked in S/4HANA due to credit limit exceeded. The standard credit limit in the migrated master data is $150K, but the customer insists they were approved for $500K years ago.

**SAP S/4HANA — Customer Master (BP 1004782)**
Name: Great Lakes Machining Corp | Credit limit: $150,000 | Credit exposure: $487,200
Status: BLOCKED — credit exceeded | Sales org: 1000
Migration note: "Migrated from ECC customer 0041200. Credit limit set per standard migration rule (highest of: legacy limit, 12-month rolling average receivables)."

**SAP ECC (archived snapshot, pre-migration) — Customer Credit Data**
Customer: 0041200 | Credit limit field (FD32): $150,000
Text field (rarely used): "See email — Rosenthal override to $500K approved 2019-06-14"

**SharePoint — /migration/cutover-decisions/credit-migration-rules.docx (v3.1, approved Aug 2024)**
Section 4.2: "Customer credit limits will be migrated as the HIGHER of: (a) the value in FD32, or (b) the trailing 12-month average A/R balance. Manual overrides documented outside the credit master will NOT be migrated unless captured in the exception spreadsheet (Appendix B)."
Appendix B: [47 rows of customer exceptions] — Customer 0041200 is NOT listed.

**Email (recovered from Outlook archive via legal hold) — Subject: "RE: Credit increase — Great Lakes Machining" (Jun 14, 2019)**
From: paul.rosenthal@ironforge.com (former CFO, retired 2022)
To: credit.team@ironforge.com
CC: plant2.controller@ironforge.com

> Approved. Raise to $500K effective immediately. They've been with us since the Dayton days and their payment history is clean. Don't make me fill out the form for this one.
> — Paul

**Microsoft Teams — #customer-escalations (Jun 24, 2026, 9:15 AM)**
@lisa.tran: Great Lakes is furious. They say their credit was $500K for years and now we're blocking their orders. I can see in ECC there's a text note about an override but nothing in S/4.
@raj.chowdhury: That's a known gap. Overrides that lived outside FD32 didn't migrate. Was it in the exception spreadsheet?
@lisa.tran: Checking... no, it wasn't.
@raj.chowdhury: Then it fell through. The old CFO approved a lot of these informally. We need the original approval evidence to reinstate.
@greg.hoffman (plant controller): I remember this one. Paul approved it over email. Let me dig it up.
[Thread continues 2 hours later]
@greg.hoffman: Found it. Forwarding to credit team now. :white_check_mark:

**Jira — MIGR-4421 (Data Governance backlog)**
Summary: "Audit informal credit overrides not captured in FD32"
Status: Open | Priority: Medium | Created: Sep 2024
Comment (Oct 2024, @raj.chowdhury): "Identified ~35 customers with text-field references to overrides. Added to data steward queue but no capacity until Q2 2026."
Comment (Jun 2026, @lisa.tran): "Great Lakes just escalated. This is now P1."
question: What is the correct resolution path for reinstating Great Lakes Machining's credit limit in S/4HANA?

contributor.name: Raj Chowdhury
contributor.title: ERP Migration & Data Governance Lead
contributor.domain_expertise: Data migration, legacy system decommissioning, master data reconciliation, cutover planning

choices: Reinstate the $500K limit using the recovered 2019 email as supporting documentation, routed through the current credit approval workflow for validation, while flagging MIGR-4421 as evidence that this was a known migration gap — not a new request
Require a brand-new credit review and approval from the current CFO since the original approver (Paul Rosenthal) has retired and his authority is no longer valid — treat this as a new credit request
Immediately reinstate the $500K limit in S/4HANA based on the ECC text field reference — the legacy system is the authoritative record and overrides should be honored without additional approval

Reject the escalation because the credit migration rules (v3.1 Section 4.2) explicitly state that overrides outside FD32 do not migrate unless in Appendix B — the customer was not listed, so the $150K limit is correct per policy
